A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same affinity-score and non-linearity-signature research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material across substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation-function experiments, measurements of pretrained vision networks, accuracy correlations, and appendix robustness and self-supervised analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds analytical-versus-empirical ReLU comparisons and experiments on randomly initialized MLPs.

M1.justification: The affine transport map (Equation 4), normalized affinity score (Equation 5), spatial averaging and covariance shrinkage are unchanged. The formal network-signature definition is shortened to prose, but no change to the underlying measurement procedure is established.

E1.justification: v4 adds a synthetic coordinate-to-scalar test scenario: randomly initialized MLPs evaluated on a 64-by-64 grid to study function complexity. The existing ImageNet, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, random-tensor and self-supervised coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator metrics, including CKA, norm, sparsity, entropy and regression R² where applicable. Accuracy correlations retain depth, parameter count and GFLOPS comparisons. The neural-redshift experiment applies the affinity score to ReLU and Tanh without introducing a competing non-linearity estimator.

E3.justification: The new MLP experiment specifies three hidden layers, uniform biases, and controlled weight ranges using s, 6s and s′ = s − 0.05. These are additional experimental settings; the retained ImageNet evaluation still uses 50,000 validation images and batches of 512.

E4.justification: v4 adds focused analyses of ReLU-score asymmetry through analytical-versus-empirical curves (Figure 3) and initialization sensitivity of ReLU/Tanh network complexity (Figure 4). Existing pooling, shrinkage, batch-size, seed, training, depth and residual-connection analyses remain.

E5.justification: The nine-seed VGG16 study, boxplots and mean/standard-deviation reporting are retained. Figure 4 adds ± values for new results, but no new statistical test, uncertainty-estimation procedure or change to stated repeated-run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 2(B) changes ReLU/Tanh/Sigmoid scores from 0.74/0.89/0.95 to 0.49/0.67/0.77, preserving their ordering without explaining the numerical revision. Figures 3–4 add results, including ReLU scores of 0.82±0.07 and 0.65±0.10 under different initialization settings. Tables 1–3 and the retained accuracy-correlation results are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 derives output moments, the affine transport map and the Wasserstein discrepancy for one-dimensional uniform inputs passed through ReLU. This is a special-case extension supporting the asymmetry analysis; the existing general theoretical statements and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal claims about the affinity score, architectural signatures, accuracy correlations and uniqueness remain. The introduction and conclusion additionally emphasize activation-domain effects on the complexity of randomly initialized MLPs.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of score asymmetry, the degenerate zero-score limit in the one-dimensional ReLU example, and initialization-dependent inductive bias. It also qualifies ResNet bimodality through activation placement. v2’s dedicated limitations discussion disappears, although theorem assumptions remain explicit and score regularization is still presented as future work.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new MLP experiment’s grid, depth, weight and bias distributions, and initialization perturbation. Appendix E also describes applying multidimensional scaling to the linkage matrix of 36 architectures. Existing implementation details and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Teney et al.’s Neural Redshift and challenges the universality of its reported ReLU simplicity bias. It also adds Glorot and Bengio’s initialization reference and Peyré and Cuturi’s optimal-transport reference, clarifying the relationship of Theorem 3.3 to Gaussian transport results.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the introductory contribution list and roadmap with a findings summary, reorganizes Section 3.2, splits and reorders architectural-similarity and residual-connection discussions, and rewrites the conclusion. It also removes the dedicated broader-impact and limitations appendices and updates author information. These changes substantially reshape the narrative despite much retained technical prose.

P2.justification: The paper changes from one-column to two-column layout and extensively regroups and resizes displays. Architecture-history, distance and density plots are combined; residual-connection plots become a separate figure. The architecture dendrogram is replaced by an appendix MDS visualization, and new Figures 3–4 present the added analyses.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.2 and Figures 3–4 improve understanding of the unchanged score through an explicit derivation and controlled initialization experiments. The findings summary and regrouped figures also clarify the presentation while retaining the main empirical evidence. These gains are limited by the loss of explicit limitations and the unexplained numerical revisions in Figure 2.
